declaration.mitigation: Operator-invoked provisioning only (management command prints DDL; nothing runs on deploy, migrate or update). Statements create a read-only definer/principal, a per-principal view database, SELECT grants and RESTRICTIVE row policies; no ALTER/DROP/INSERT on existing tables, no data rewrite. Rollback: DROP the created users, row policies and view database.

Metadata-only ALTER TABLE spans MODIFY COLUMN trace_name (expression change, type unchanged): no mutation, no data rewritten (rehearsed on CH 25.3: system.mutations count unchanged). Removes the trace_dict lookup from the span insert path. Never run MATERIALIZE COLUMN trace_name afterwards. Rollback: app code rolls back alone; restoring the dictionary expression needs a new forward schema file.

Fresh OSS installs create spans.trace_name with the row-local root expression; retained installs are inspect-only and now accept the new, the legacy 015 and the qualified legacy expression, rejecting anything else. No DDL on retained tables.
Drops the guard that required exactly one trace_dict reference in the spans trace_name override; trace_dict is still created and 015's statement counts are unchanged. No DDL on retained tables.

Removes --materialize-spans (would blank stored names via a full mutation) and the default SYSTEM RELOAD DICTIONARY trace_dict (re-triggers the double-copy load). The command now only writes traces rows as before.
